- When sentiment is consistently high (>0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% above recent high; avoid overcorrection after spike.
- If sentiment is low (<0.4) and price is trending down, model often underestimates decline; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) after volatility spikes; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If sentiment is rising steadily, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slightly (1–3%) to reflect sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment divergence.
